text: 代理开关 · dsh-proxy-switch 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的网页抓取线路插件。它接管 web_fetch 的 HTTP provider，并通过独立的本机转发通道，在自动、代理和直连模式间选择；自动模式会探测本机代理，也可手动设置 HTTP 代理。侧栏、对话顶栏和插件设置页提供状态、线路、代理地址及作用范围控制，适合使用 Clash、Surge 等本机 HTTP 代理的 DSH 用户。需要 DSH 桌面环境和可用的本机 HTTP 代理；没有 API key 配置项。

Proxy Switch routes DSH web_fetch through a local HTTP proxy or direct connection. It detects the proxy automatically and offers manual route and address controls. Its sidebar, chat header, and plugin page show status and settings. For DSH users with a local HTTP proxy; no API key is needed.
DSH 抓网页时遇到代理或 fake-IP 问题，能自动切换本机 HTTP 代理和直连吗？
Can DSH web_fetch follow my local proxy when it is running and go direct when it is off?
dsh-proxy-switch 的功能「web_fetch 代理切换」：自动模式根据本机代理探测结果选择代理或直连，也可固定选择一种线路；网页抓取请求经独立 provider 和本机转发通道发出。

**开着 Clash、Surge、v2rayN 这类代理软件时，DeepSeek Harness 的 `web_fetch` 抓不了网页？装上这个插件就好了。**

它会自动找到你电脑上的代理，代理开着就让 `web_fetch` 走代理，关着就直连。不用改 `.env`，也不用记端口号。

[环境要求](#环境要求) · [安装](#安装) · [怎么用](#怎么用) · [看到提示怎么办](#看到提示怎么办) · [常见问题](#常见问题) · [工作原理](#工作原理) ---

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 它解决什么问题：如果你遇到过下面任何一种情况，这个插件就是为你写的： - `web_fetch` 报错 **`non-public IP address`**，或者提示网站被解析到 **`198.18.x.x`**； - 代理软件开了 **TUN / 增强模式 / fake-IP**，DeepSeek 一抓网页就失败； - 只在代理软件里打开了「系统代理」、没开 TUN：DSH 不读系统代理，`web_fetch` 打不开需要代理的网站； - 为了让 `web_fetch` 能用，把 `HTTP_PROXY` 写死进了 `~/.dsh/.env`，结果代理一关，**连模型对话都断了**； - 每次开关代理都要手动改配置。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 它解决什么问题：原因在于：TUN 模式的代理会把所有域名解析成 `198.18.0.0/15` 段的"假地址"。`web_fetch` 直连时的安全检查不允许访问内网地址，于是把请求拒绝了；而一旦把代理写死，代理关掉后又什么都连不上。这个插件给 `web_fetch` 单独开了一条可以切换的线路，**默认不影响模型对话和其它功能**。

> DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2 起，`web_fetch` 不再拒绝 fake-IP 和内网地址，只用 TUN 的话新版不装插件也能抓网页。插件仍然适合：只开系统代理的用户、需要代理开关时自动切换的用户；直连时插件仍只允许公网地址，可以挡住对本机和内网服务的访问。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 安装：在 DeepSeek Harness 里对模型说：「用 plugin_manager 安装插件 `@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch`」，然后**完全退出并重新打开 DSH**。侧栏底部右边会多出一个小按钮，显示当前线路和状态圆点（如「走代理 ●」）。

> 以前在 `~/.dsh/.env` 里写过 `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` 的话，先删掉它们再重启。否则插件关掉后，DSH 还会回到写死的代理。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 安装：1. 下载源码：
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch.git ~/dsh-proxy-switch

3. 完全退出并重新打开 DSH。升级时在源码目录 `git pull`，再执行一次第 2、3 步。

从 0.4.1 及更早版本升级时（0.4.2 起包名改为 `@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch`），先让模型用 `plugin_manager` 卸载 `dsh-proxy-switch`，再按上面的方法安装新版；设置和状态会保留。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 怎么用：| 位置 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **最上面一大块** | 现在走的是哪条线路。线条在流动表示通畅；出问题时，符号标在出问题的地方：✕ 表示那里断了，🔒 表示代理要登录，❗ 加时断时续的线表示不稳定（部分网站会失败）；灰线上有光点在扫表示正在检测。右上角的小标签是作用范围：「仅 web_fetch」或「所有工具」。 |
| **自动 / 走代理 / 直连** | 选线路。「自动」适合绝大多数人；另外两个会把线路固定住，不管代理开没开。 |
| **代理那一行** | 找到的代理地址、怎么找到的（系统代理、环境变量或端口扫描），以及延迟。右边的按钮可以重新检测。 |
| **更多设置** | 手动填写代理地址、作用范围、按钮放在哪里。 |

按钮上的圆点：🟢 正常，🟠 需要处理，🔴 出现问题，⚪ 正在检测。
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 按钮放哪里：左侧栏底部可能挤着好几个插件按钮。在「更多设置 → 按钮位置」里可以选： - **侧栏底部**（默认） - **对话顶栏**：适合侧栏常收起的人。Windows 上侧栏收起时，底部这一行会被隐藏。 - **不显示**：所有设置都还在「**插件 → 代理开关**」页面里，随时可以回来改。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 看到提示怎么办：线路和代理状态对不上时，面板会给出一句话说明和一个修复按钮，点按钮就行。
代理客户端正在运行：你固定了直连，但代理开着，部分网站会被拒绝。点「改为自动」。 找不到代理的端口：代理似乎在运行，但它没有设置系统代理，端口也不常见。点「手动填写地址」，只填端口号（例如 7890）就行。
其它提示也一样，按按钮上写的做即可。`web_fetch` 的结果里也会附上同样的提示，模型能看到并告诉你。
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 会影响模型对话、搜索或者其它工具吗？：默认不会。作用范围是「仅 web_fetch」，插件不修改全局网络设置、进程环境变量和子进程环境。只有你主动选择「所有工具」时，其它模块才会跟着走这条线路。
section: 会影响模型对话、搜索或者其它工具吗？

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 我的代理软件端口不是 7890，能找到吗？：能。插件优先读取**系统代理设置**（macOS 的网络设置、Windows 的 Internet 选项、Linux 的 GNOME/KDE 代理设置），所以无论什么端口，只要代理软件打开了「系统代理」就能找到。找不到时会再读取 DSH 启动时的 `HTTPS_PROXY` 等环境变量，最后扫描常见端口（7890、7897、6152、1087、10809 等）。每个候选地址都会实际握手验证，确认它真的是 HTTP 代理才会使用。
section: 我的代理软件端口不是 7890，能找到吗？

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 自动模式会不会切错？：每次 `web_fetch` 之前，插件会先在本机测一下代理端口（只需约 1 毫秒），所以代理刚关掉也不会走错线路。代理找不到时一律直连，直连的安全检查照常进行。
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 代理需要账号密码怎么办？：自动检测会发现它要求登录，并提示你手动填写 `http://user:pass@地址:端口`。密码只保存在本机，权限为 600，界面、日志和提示里一律显示为 `***`。
section: 代理需要账号密码怎么办？

text:
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 走代理时，模型能借插件访问我的内网或本机服务吗？：插件会尽量挡住，但不能保证百分之百。走代理时，网址最终由代理软件去解析和连接，插件看不到它实际连到了哪里。所以插件在交给代理之前先在本机检查一遍：`localhost`、`.local`、`.lan` 这类本地名字直接拒绝，在本机解析出内网地址的也拒绝。但开着 TUN 时本机只能解析到假地址（`198.18.x.x`），判断不了真实目标，只能放行。这和以前在 `~/.dsh/.env` 里手写 `HTTP_PROXY` 时的情况一样；直连则有完整的检查。

反过来，如果你的 DNS 被污染，把正常网站解析成了内网地址，走代理时这个网站会被误拒，提示里会写「转发模式拒绝请求」。打开代理软件的 TUN（或换一个可信的 DNS）就能恢复。
section: 走代理时，模型能借插件访问我的内网或本机服务吗？

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 支持 SOCKS、HTTPS 或 PAC 代理吗？：目前只支持 HTTP 代理。好在几乎所有代理软件都提供 HTTP 端口或"混合端口"，用那个端口就行。
section: 支持 SOCKS、HTTPS 或 PAC 代理吗？

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 支持 Windows、Linux 吗？：代码按三个平台编写，自动检测会分别读取各自的系统代理设置，但目前只在 macOS 上完整验证过。欢迎反馈。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 工作原理：```
web_fetch ──▶ 插件自己的 web_fetch 提供者 ──▶ 本机私有通道（随机端口，只监听 127.0.0.1）
                                                ├─ 走代理：CONNECT / 绝对 URI ──▶ 你的 HTTP 代理
                                                └─ 直连：  解析 DNS + 安全检查 ──▶ 目标网站
```

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 工作原理：- 插件只替换 `web_fetch` 的"发请求"这一步。重定向、超时、大小限制、编码处理仍然沿用 DSH 原来的实现。
- 直连时，整组 DNS 结果都必须是公网地址：fake-IP、内网、回环、NAT64 内嵌私网地址等一律拒绝。
- 走代理时，本地名字和在本机解析成内网地址的目标会被拒绝；最终由代理解析，所以这只是缓解（见上面的常见问题）。
- 私有通道每次启动生成随机令牌，本机其它程序无法借用它（以及你保存的代理账号密码）。
- 每个请求都使用新连接，切换线路后不会沿用旧的代理隧道。
- 设计细节、安全边界和测试覆盖见 [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)。历史审查记录见 [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md)。
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 配置与状态文件：面板里能改的设置都保存在 `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-proxy-switch/state.json`（目录权限 0700、文件权限 0600）。一般不需要手动编辑。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 配置与状态文件：| 字段 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `auto` | `auto`（跟随检测结果）/ `forward`（固定走代理）/ `direct`（固定直连） |
| `upstreamSource` | `auto` | `auto` 时代理地址由检测结果更新；`manual` 时只使用你填写的地址 |
| `upstream` | `http://127.0.0.1:1082` | 代理地址，只接受 `http://host:port`，可以带 `user:pass@` |
| `scope` | `web_fetch_only` | `web_fetch_only`（仅 web_fetch）/ `global`（所有工具） |
| `listenPort` | `7899` | 仅「所有工具」模式使用的本地端口 |
| `probeIntervalMs` | `15000` | 后台检测代理的间隔（3000–600000 毫秒），界面里不提供修改 |

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 配置与状态文件：按钮位置是浏览器端的偏好，保存在 `localStorage` 的 `dsh-proxy-switch.placement` 里。

从 0.3 升级时，原来的线路选择会保留。原来的代理地址如果是默认值，会改为自动检测；如果是你填写过的地址，会保持手动。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 状态接口：接口只接受本机请求，`Host` 必须是 DSH 自己的地址，并校验 `Origin`、`Sec-Fetch-Site`；`POST` 还要求 `Content-Type: application/json` 和请求头 `x-dsh-proxy-switch-request: 1`。`state` 里的主要字段有：`mode`、`effectiveMode`（当前实际走的线路）、`upstream`（已脱敏）、`upstreamSource`、`detection`、`probe`、`warning`、`provider`、`scope`、`stats`。

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 开发与测试：```bash
npm test                                   # 单元测试（含 Client 渲染测试）
DSH_RUNTIME_MODULES=/path/to/dsh/node_modules node scripts/e2e-host.mjs   # 真实 Cordis/WebRuntime 集成测试
node scripts/e2e-real.mjs                  # 可选：经过本机真实 HTTP 代理
node scripts/e2e-web-fetch-warning.mjs     # web_fetch 结果附带的警告文本

`DSH_RUNTIME_MODULES` 指向 DSH 运行时的 `node_modules`。可以从安装包里解出来：`npx @electron/asar extract "/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar" out`，然后使用 `out/dsh/node_modules`。
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · 开发与测试：依赖必须写在 `peerDependencies` 里，不能写进 `dependencies`，否则会装出第二份 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-http-proxy`，「所有工具」模式会静默失效。

**Does DeepSeek Harness `web_fetch` stop working while Clash, Surge or v2rayN is running? This plugin fixes it.**

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Proxy Switch · dsh-proxy-switch：It finds the proxy on your computer by itself. While the proxy runs, `web_fetch` goes through it; when the proxy is off, `web_fetch` goes direct. No `.env` editing, no port numbers to remember.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Proxy Switch · dsh-proxy-switch：[Requirements](#requirements) · [Install](#install) · [Usage](#usage) · [When a notice appears](#when-a-notice-appears) · [FAQ](#faq) · [How it works](#how-it-works)

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · What problem it solves：

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · What problem it solves：Why it happens: a proxy in TUN mode answers every DNS lookup with a "fake" address in `198.18.0.0/15`. When `web_fetch` connects directly, its safety check refuses private addresses, so the request is rejected. Hard-coding the proxy fixes that, until the proxy is turned off and nothing connects at all. This plugin gives `web_fetch` its own switchable route. **By default, model calls and other features are not affected.**

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · What problem it solves：> Since DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2, `web_fetch` no longer refuses fake-IP and private addresses, so with TUN alone the new version fetches pages without this plugin. The plugin still fits users who only enable the system proxy and users who want `web_fetch` to switch automatically with the proxy; in direct mode it still allows public addresses only, which keeps requests away from services on this machine and the local network.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Requirements：| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek Harness | Desktop 0.2.1 and 0.2.2 (0.2.2-rc.1 tested) |
| System | macOS (fully verified); Windows and Linux (supported in code, not yet fully verified on real machines) |
| Proxy | A local HTTP proxy or "mixed port" (Clash / mihomo / Clash Verge, Surge, v2rayN all provide one). SOCKS and PAC are not supported |
| License | [MIT](LICENSE) |

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Install：In DeepSeek Harness, ask the model: "Install the plugin `@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch` with plugin_manager", then **quit DSH completely and open it again**. A small pill appears at the bottom right of the sidebar, showing the current route and a status dot (for example "Proxy ●").

> If you previously put `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` in `~/.dsh/.env`, remove them before restarting. Otherwise DSH falls back to the hard-coded proxy whenever the plugin is off.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Install：<details>
<summary>Install from source (if you want to change the code)</summary>

1. Get the source:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch.git ~/dsh-proxy-switch
   ```
2. Ask the model: "Install the plugin at `~/dsh-proxy-switch` with plugin_manager" (it runs `plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=<absolute path>`).
3. Quit DSH completely and open it again. To upgrade, run `git pull` in the source folder and repeat steps 2 and 3.
</details>

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Install：When upgrading from 0.4.1 or earlier (0.4.2 renames the package to `@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch`), first ask the model to uninstall `dsh-proxy-switch` with `plugin_manager`, then install the new version as above. Your settings and state are kept.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Usage：**Most people do not need to do anything.** The default is **Auto**: the plugin reads your system proxy settings, finds the proxy port, routes `web_fetch` through the proxy while it runs, and switches to direct when the proxy is turned off.

Click the pill at the bottom of the sidebar to open the panel:

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Usage：| Part | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **The large card at the top** | The route in use right now. A flowing line means traffic gets through. When something is wrong, a mark sits where the problem is: ✕ means that hop is broken, 🔒 means the proxy wants a login, ❗ with a stuttering line means the route is unreliable (some sites will fail). A glint sweeping a grey line means it is checking. The tag in the top right is the scope: *web_fetch only* or *All tools*. |
| **Auto / Proxy / Direct** | Choose the route. **Auto** suits almost everyone; the other two pin the route regardless of whether the proxy is running. |
| **The proxy line** | The proxy address it found, how it was found (system proxy, environment variable or port scan), and the latency. The button on the right checks again. |
| **More settings** | Enter a proxy address yourself, change the scope, choose where the button lives. |
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Usage：The dot on the pill: 🟢 fine, 🟠 needs attention, 🔴 something is wrong, ⚪ checking.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Where the button lives：The bottom of the sidebar can get crowded with plugin buttons. Under **More settings → Button location** you can choose:

- **Sidebar** (default)
- **Chat header**: handy if you usually keep the sidebar collapsed. On Windows, this footer row is hidden while the sidebar is collapsed.
- **Hidden**: every setting is still on the **Plugins → Proxy Switch** page.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Where the button lives：The plugin page has the full panel and every setting. *(The screenshots below show the Chinese interface; the plugin follows the DSH language setting.)*
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · When a notice appears：When the route and the proxy disagree, the panel explains it in one sentence and offers a button that fixes it. Click the button.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · When a notice appears：
Your proxy app is running: you pinned Direct, but the proxy is on, so some sites will be refused. Click Switch to Auto. Proxy port not found: the proxy seems to be running, but it does not set the system proxy and its port is not a common one. Click Enter the address; a port number alone (for example 7890) is enough.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · When a notice appears：Other notices work the same way: do what the button says. The same notice is also appended to `web_fetch` results, so the model sees it and can tell you.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Does it affect model calls, search or other tools?：Not by default. The scope is *web_fetch only*: the plugin does not change global network settings, the process environment or child-process environments. Other modules use this route only if you choose *All tools*.
section: Does it affect model calls, search or other tools?

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · My proxy app does not use port 7890. Will it be found?：Yes. The plugin reads the **system proxy settings** first (Network settings on macOS, Internet Options on Windows, GNOME/KDE proxy settings on Linux), so any port works as long as your proxy app has "system proxy" turned on. Otherwise it reads `HTTPS_PROXY`-style variables from the DSH launch environment, and finally scans common ports (7890, 7897, 6152, 1087, 10809 and others). Each candidate is verified with a real `CONNECT` handshake and used only if it answers like an HTTP proxy.
section: My proxy app does not use port 7890. Will it be found?

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Can Auto pick the wrong route?：Before each `web_fetch`, the plugin checks the proxy port locally (about 1 ms), so it will not keep using the proxy right after you turn it off. If no proxy is found, it goes direct, and the direct-mode safety check still applies.
section: Can Auto pick the wrong route?

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · What if my proxy needs a username and password?：Detection notices that the proxy asks for a login, and the panel asks you to enter `http://user:pass@host:port` yourself. The password is stored only on this computer with file mode 600, and is shown as `***` in the interface, logs and notices.
section: What if my proxy needs a username and password?

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · In proxy mode, could the model use the plugin to reach my local network?：The plugin blocks what it can, but it cannot guarantee it. In proxy mode, your proxy app resolves the name and makes the connection, so the plugin cannot see where it finally goes. Before handing a request to the proxy, the plugin checks it locally: local names such as `localhost`, `.local` and `.lan` are refused, and so are names that resolve to a private address on this computer. With TUN on, however, this computer only sees fake addresses (`198.18.x.x`), so the real target cannot be judged and the request is allowed. This is the same exposure you had with a hard-coded `HTTP_PROXY` in `~/.dsh/.env`. Direct mode checks every DNS answer.
section: In proxy mode, could the model use the plugin to reach my local network?

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · In proxy mode, could the model use the plugin to reach my local network?：The other way round: if your DNS is polluted and answers a normal site with a private address, proxy mode will refuse that site by mistake, and the notice says *Forward mode refused …*. Turning on your proxy app's TUN (or switching to a trusted DNS) fixes it.
section: In proxy mode, could the model use the plugin to reach my local network?

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Are SOCKS, HTTPS or PAC proxies supported?：Only HTTP proxies for now. Almost every proxy app offers an HTTP port or a "mixed port"; use that one.
section: Are SOCKS, HTTPS or PAC proxies supported?

text: @lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Does it work on Windows and Linux?：The code covers all three platforms, and detection reads each system's proxy settings, but so far it has been fully verified only on macOS. Feedback is welcome.
section: Does it work on Windows and Linux?

text:
@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · How it works：```
web_fetch ──▶ the plugin's own web_fetch provider ──▶ private local channel (random port, 127.0.0.1 only)
                                                      ├─ Proxy:  CONNECT / absolute URI ──▶ your HTTP proxy
                                                      └─ Direct: DNS + safety check ──────▶ the website
```

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · How it works：- The plugin replaces only the "send the request" step of `web_fetch`. Redirects, timeouts, size limits and decoding still use DSH's own implementation.
- In direct mode, every DNS answer must be a public address: fake IPs, private, loopback and NAT64-embedded private addresses are all refused.
- In proxy mode, local names and targets that resolve to a private address on this computer are refused. The proxy resolves the name in the end, so this is a mitigation (see the FAQ above).
- The private channel uses a random token generated at each start, so other programs on this computer cannot use it, or the proxy credentials you saved.
- Every request opens a new connection, so a route change never reuses an old proxy tunnel.
- Design details, security boundaries and test coverage: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) (Chinese). Earlier review notes: [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md).

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Settings file：Everything you can change in the panel is saved in `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-proxy-switch/state.json` (folder mode 0700, file mode 0600). You normally never need to edit it.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Settings file：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `auto` | `auto` (follow detection) / `forward` (always use the proxy) / `direct` (always go direct) |
| `upstreamSource` | `auto` | `auto`: the proxy address follows detection; `manual`: only the address you entered is used |
| `upstream` | `http://127.0.0.1:1082` | Proxy address. Only `http://host:port` is accepted, optionally with `user:pass@` |
| `scope` | `web_fetch_only` | `web_fetch_only` / `global` (all tools) |
| `listenPort` | `7899` | Local port used only by the *All tools* scope |
| `probeIntervalMs` | `15000` | How often the proxy is checked in the background (3000–600000 ms); not shown in the interface |

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Settings file：The button location is a browser-side preference, stored in `localStorage` as `dsh-proxy-switch.placement`.

When upgrading from 0.3, your route choice is kept. A proxy address left at the old default switches to automatic detection; an address you entered stays manual.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · State API：The routes accept only local requests whose `Host` is DSH's own address, and check `Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Site`. `POST` also requires `Content-Type: application/json` and the header `x-dsh-proxy-switch-request: 1`. Main fields in `state`: `mode`, `effectiveMode` (the route in use), `upstream` (credentials masked), `upstreamSource`, `detection`, `probe`, `warning`, `provider`, `scope`, `stats`.

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Development and tests：```bash
npm test                                   # unit tests (including client rendering)
DSH_RUNTIME_MODULES=/path/to/dsh/node_modules node scripts/e2e-host.mjs   # integration tests on the real Cordis/WebRuntime
node scripts/e2e-real.mjs                  # optional: through a real local HTTP proxy
node scripts/e2e-web-fetch-warning.mjs     # the notice text appended to web_fetch results

@lightrivers/dsh-proxy-switch README · Development and tests：`DSH_RUNTIME_MODULES` points at the DSH runtime's `node_modules`. You can extract it from the app: `npx @electron/asar extract "/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar" out`, then use `out/dsh/node_modules`.

Runtime packages must stay in `peerDependencies`, never `dependencies`; a second copy of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-http-proxy` would make the *All tools* scope fail silently.
